types.label: Technical Support
types.intro: Follow a repair call from the opening to a confirmed fix. The steps that drive repeat contacts and transfers are marked, so you can see where aiCR and transfer risk came from.

steps.title: Open and acknowledge
steps.good: Greet the customer, restate the reason for the call, and acknowledge how the issue is affecting them before anything else.
steps.say: I'm sorry the internet keeps dropping while you're working from home. Let's find out what's causing it.

steps.title: Verify the account
steps.good: Complete account verification following the applicable process before discussing or changing anything on the account.

steps.title: Discover and scope
steps.good: Ask when the issue started, which devices and services are affected, and what the customer has already tried.
steps.say: When did you first notice the drops, and is it happening on every device or just one?

steps.title: Check history and outages
steps.good: Review previous contacts and check for known outages before starting troubleshooting, so a repeat issue is treated as one.

steps.title: Follow the ITG
steps.good: Work through the applicable ITG flow step by step, without skipping steps or improvising a different path.

steps.title: Keep the customer informed
steps.good: Explain what you are checking and how long it will take, and use the hold process correctly for longer research.
steps.say: I'm going to check the signal history on your equipment. That will take about two minutes. Is it okay if I place you on a brief hold?

steps.title: Fix the root cause
steps.good: Identify the actual cause and resolve it, rather than treating a symptom or replacing equipment by default.

steps.title: Own it before you route it
steps.good: Resolve what you can yourself. When a transfer or technician visit is truly needed, follow the correct path and process.

steps.title: Set clear expectations
steps.good: Explain what happens next, including appointment or outage details, without guaranteeing an outcome you cannot confirm.

steps.title: Confirm the fix and close
steps.good: Have the customer confirm the service works on their side, recap what was done, and close the call warmly.
steps.say: Could you open a page on your laptop and tell me if it loads normally now?

skills.title: Clear technical explanations
skills.good: Explain each technical step in plain language and check that the customer can follow along.

skills.title: Tools navigation
skills.good: Move through the tools efficiently, so research time stays short and the customer is not left waiting.

skills.title: Call control
skills.good: Guide the conversation with purpose and keep the call moving toward the fix.

skills.title: Tone and energy
skills.good: Keep a warm, confident, engaged tone from the opening to the close, even during long troubleshooting.

skills.title: Customer education
skills.good: Show the customer what to do if the issue returns, so they are not left needing to call again.

types.label: Billing
types.intro: Review a billing call from the first acknowledgement to a customer who understands the next bill. Accurate expectations here are what prevent repeat contacts.

steps.title: Open and acknowledge
steps.good: Greet the customer and restate the billing concern in your own words, so they know you understood it.

steps.title: Acknowledge the frustration
steps.good: Recognize how an unexpected bill feels for the customer before explaining any charges.
steps.say: I can see why a higher bill than you expected is frustrating. Let's go through it together so it makes sense.

steps.title: Verify the account
steps.good: Complete account verification following the applicable process before discussing account details.

steps.title: Review the account and history
steps.good: Review the statement, recent changes, and any previous billing commitments before answering the question.

steps.title: Explain the bill
steps.good: Walk through each charge that changed and why, in plain language and in a logical order.
steps.say: There are two changes on this bill. Let's start with the first one, and I'll explain what changed and why.

steps.title: Offer the right options
steps.good: Explain the payment or plan options that fit the customer's situation, using approved resources.

steps.title: Set accurate expectations
steps.good: Be accurate about any credit, refund, payment, or service restoration, and never promise what you cannot confirm.

steps.title: Disclose pricing fully
steps.good: Disclose pricing completely, including when a promotional rate ends and what the standard rate will be afterward.

steps.title: Recognize cancellation risk
steps.good: Notice when the customer mentions cancelling or switching, and address the concern behind it before routing anywhere.

steps.title: Educate and confirm
steps.good: Check that the customer understands what the next bill will look like, then recap the call.
steps.say: Before we finish, can you tell me what you expect to see on next month's bill, so I know I explained it clearly?

skills.title: Clear explanations
skills.good: Use plain language and short steps, and avoid billing jargon the customer may not know.

skills.title: De-escalation
skills.good: Stay calm and steady when the customer is upset, and move the conversation toward a solution.

skills.title: Ownership
skills.good: Handle the billing concern yourself whenever you can, instead of passing it to another team.

skills.title: Research with updates
skills.good: Tell the customer what you are reviewing and how long it will take while you look at the account.

skills.title: Tone and pace
skills.good: Keep a patient, professional tone and a pace the customer can follow.

types.label: Customer Service
types.intro: A general customer service review for any call type. It follows the conversation from the opening to a confirmed resolution, with ownership and transfers marked.

steps.title: Strong opening
steps.good: Open with energy, introduce yourself, and move quickly to the reason for the call.

steps.title: Empathize
steps.good: Respond to how the situation is affecting the customer, using details they actually shared.
steps.say: Having your service go down right before an important meeting is stressful. I'm glad you called, and I'll help you with it now.

steps.title: Assure
steps.good: Tell the customer clearly that you will take care of the concern, and preview the first step.

steps.title: Listen and discover
steps.good: Let the customer finish, ask open questions, and confirm what they need before acting.

steps.title: Find the main concern
steps.good: Identify the main reason for the call and check previous contacts, so the real issue gets solved.

steps.title: Research with updates
steps.good: Give an estimate before research, use hold correctly, and check back with updates when it takes longer.

steps.title: Resolve it fully
steps.good: Resolve the primary concern completely, and take ownership instead of handing off what you can handle.

steps.title: Route only when needed
steps.good: Transfer or escalate only when the issue truly needs another team, and follow the warm transfer steps when you do.

steps.title: Set expectations and follow up
steps.good: Explain what happens next and keep any callback or follow-up commitment through the applicable process.

steps.title: Confirm and close
steps.good: Confirm the issue is resolved from the customer's side, recap the call, and close warmly.
steps.say: Just to recap, we updated your plan and the change shows on your account now. Is there anything else I can help with today?

skills.title: Rapport
skills.good: Make a genuine connection using what the customer shares, while keeping the call on track.

skills.title: Tone and energy
skills.good: Sound warm, engaged, and confident from the opening to the close.

skills.title: Clear explanations
skills.good: Explain steps and outcomes simply, and check that the customer is following.

skills.title: De-escalation
skills.good: Stay calm with an upset customer, own the experience, and move the conversation toward a solution.

skills.title: Call control
skills.good: Keep the call organized, avoid asking for the same information twice, and lead it toward resolution.
